title: Liner Notes
desc: Buried in the credits, contractual absurdity & the instruments you've never heard of

questions.q: Max Martin has written more #1 Billboard hits than any songwriter since The Beatles. Name three artists he's written for.
questions.a: Britney Spears, Backstreet Boys, NSYNC, Katy Perry, Taylor Swift, The Weeknd, Ariana Grande — among many others

questions.q: What is a 'sample clearance' and which hip-hop lawsuit in the 1990s changed the rules forever?
questions.a: Legal permission to reuse another artist's recording. Grand Upright Music vs Warner Bros (1991) — Biz Markie used a Gilbert O'Sullivan sample without clearance and lost, making uncleared sampling legally dangerous

questions.q: The didgeridoo is one of the oldest instruments still played. How old is it estimated to be?
questions.a: At least 1,500 years, possibly up to 40,000 years — indigenous Australian rock art depicts it

questions.q: What is 'sidechain compression' and why does it make dance music pump?
questions.a: The kick drum signal triggers compression on the bass/synths, briefly ducking their volume on each beat — creating the signature 'breathing' effect in EDM

questions.q: Prince changed his name to a symbol in the 1990s. Why?
questions.a: A contract dispute with Warner Bros — he couldn't release music under 'Prince' due to his deal, so he became an unpronounceable symbol (Love Symbol) to work around it

questions.q: What are 'overtones' and why does a violin sound different from a flute playing the same note?
questions.a: Every instrument produces the fundamental frequency plus additional harmonic frequencies at different intensities — this unique blend is called 'timbre' and it's why each instrument has a distinct voice

questions.q: Which album has spent the most total weeks on the Billboard 200 chart?
questions.a: 'The Dark Side of the Moon' by Pink Floyd — over 950 weeks (roughly 18 years on the chart, non-consecutively)

questions.q: What is a 'tritone' and why was it called 'the devil's interval' in medieval times?
questions.a: An interval of three whole tones (e.g. C to F#) — it sounds dissonant and unsettling. The Catholic Church reportedly discouraged its use, calling it 'diabolus in musica'

questions.q: Joni Mitchell's 'Both Sides Now' was recorded by her three times across how many years?
questions.a: About 33 years — the last version (2000) is dramatically different, reflecting decades of life experience in a slower, orchestral arrangement

questions.q: What physical format outsold vinyl for the first time in 1988?
questions.a: The CD — compact discs overtook vinyl records in sales, beginning vinyl's decline until its recent revival
